claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?** If so, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim for my son Alex. He's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm assessing eligibility for your son Alex, who is 6 years old.

Before I can determine eligibility, I need to understand your circumstances better.

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's helpful.

Now I need to understand a bit more about your residency and immigration status, as this affects Child Benefit eligibility.

**What is your residency status in the UK? Are you a British citizen, or do you have a different immigration status (such as settled status, visa, etc.)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK - I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for clarifying that.

I have one more important question to help me assess your eligibility:

**Are you currently working or receiving any income? And if so, is your income above or below the Child Benefit income limit?** 

(For context, there's an income threshold above which Child Benefit is affected, but I want to understand your situation first.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I do work, yes. Could you tell me what the income limit is? I'm not sure if I'm above or below it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course, let me check the official eligibility criteria to give you the accurate information about income limits.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I can see the main eligibility page, but I need to check for more specific information about the income limit. Let me search the other relevant pages as well to ensure I have complete information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. Based on the official guidance I've reviewed, I can clarify the income situation:

**Good news:** You can claim Child Benefit regardless of your income level. However, there is an important rule called the **High Income Child Benefit Tax Charge**. 

If you or your partner have an individual income over **£60,000 per year**, you may have to pay a tax charge on the Child Benefit you receive. This doesn't prevent you from claiming - you'll still receive the benefit, but you may need to pay back some or all of it through tax.

So, to help me complete my assessment:

**Does your income (or your partner's income, if you have one) exceed £60,000 per year?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, my income is well below that - I don't earn anywhere near £60,000.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for clarifying that. That means the High Income Child Benefit Tax Charge won't apply to you.

Now I have just one more question to complete my assessment:

**Are there any other circumstances affecting Alex that I should know about? For example, is he currently in hospital, care, or residential accommodation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. He's just a normal 6-year-old living at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the eligibility criteria, you meet all the requirements:

✓ You're responsible for Alex (he lives with you)
✓ Alex is under 16 years old
✓ You live in the UK
✓ You're a British citizen
✓ Your income is below the £60,000 threshold
✓ Alex is not in hospital or care

You should be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Let me now provide you with my formal assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: **Summary:** You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for your son Alex. You can proceed with making a claim through HMRC. If you have any further questions about the application process, HMRC's Child Benefit Office will be able to assist you.

All eligibility criteria are met.
